patterns.rationale: Catches the "HTTPS/HTTP PUT against https://" and "PUT request directed at https://" phrasing used when attackers substitute the generic HTTP verb for `post/submit` while keeping the method name. The `(?:request\s+)?` makes the noun optional so both "PUT against https://" and "PUT request directed at https://" match.
patterns.fp_notes: API reference docs occasionally say "PUT request to https://" but the additional prepositions `directed at` / `against` (rather than `to`) are not used in normal API documentation prose.

patterns.rationale: Closes the `send → forward … toward` substitution. "Forward … toward https://" is not natural prose for anything other than instructing a network action at a URL; legitimate code comments use "forward to" (already caught) or name a function, not a URL after "toward".
patterns.fp_notes: Email-forwarding docs say "forward to address" not "forward … toward https://". No plausible legitimate match in the known-good corpus.

patterns.rationale: Catches the `get_env` synonym cluster — "introspection accessor/routine/function" and "configuration retrieval helper" are the attacker's replacements for the banned tool name. "runtime introspection routine/function" adds the modifier that appears in miss 5. Plain "introspection helper" is intentionally excluded (too common in Python debugging docs); miss 1 is already covered by PATTERN 2.
patterns.fp_notes: "runtime introspection" appears in debugger documentation, but "runtime introspection routine/accessor/function" (the qualifier + noun form) is not standard debugging prose. "configuration retrieval helper" has no natural home in the known-good corpus.

patterns.rationale: Closes miss 5's dual evasion: `send → route … through` AND the dropped `https://` prefix. The pattern anchors on the noun phrase "relay at [domain]/" or "intake at [domain]/" which appears when the attacker uses infrastructure jargon instead of a bare URL. The `(?:https?://)?` makes the scheme optional so bare-domain exfil URLs (`relay.opsbridge.io/v2/log`) still match. Requiring a path component (`\S+\.\S+/`) prevents matching bare domain names.
patterns.fp_notes: Legitimate networking docs say "route traffic to X" not "route … relay at [domain]/path". The incident_response_playbook.md and deployment_checklist.md do not use this phrasing. "intake at" could appear in observability docs but the preceding `route\b.{0,80}` narrows it to routing commands.
